html:
Pamoari is probably a spelling of the Paumari, an Arawan speaking people of the middle Purus River in Amazonas, Brazil, around Lábrea and Tapauá, where this territory lies.

The Paumari are a river people who once lived much of the year in floating houses on the lakes and side channels of the Purus, fishing and hunting turtles and manatees. The Amazon rubber boom in the late 1800s brought rubber tappers onto the Purus, and many Paumari were drawn into debt work for them. They number in the low thousands today. Their neighbours include the Apurinã.
